issue.title: Remote F fork launches a local agent: _submit_launch_proc's 'Fork on ' display-name intercept never matches
issue.description: Found while consolidating research.46 (MacBook as main SASE TUI over remote agents); verified by code reading at sase `9fd8a081f4`. Root cause is precise: the remote-fork interception in `_submit_launch_proc` matches `display_name.startswith("Fork on ")`, but all callers prefix the display name with `launch `/`check launch `, so the branch is dead and the fork prompt launches locally. See the consolidated report's §2.1 #1.

task_type_fields.impact: Remote fork silently runs on the wrong machine. On a low-resource controller (the planned MacBook viewer) this launches a heavy local agent instead of an owner-side `lifecycle.fork`, with no error. Docs and three of five research reports describe remote fork as working. Fix: carry an explicit launch-context flag (not a display-name prefix) from the remote fork prompt bar to submission, clear the pending identity on cancel/submit, and add a test that drives the real prompt-bar submit path and asserts `_submit_remote_fork` is called and no local launch proc is created.
task_type_fields.repro:
1. In the ACE Agents tab, select a remote fleet row (`fleet_origin_alias` set, e.g. an apollo agent) and press `F`.
2. `action_fork_agent` (`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_fork_actions.py:107-123`) opens a prompt bar with `display_name="Fork on <alias>"` and records `_pending_remote_fork_identity`.
3. Type a fork instruction and submit.
4. The launch reaches `_submit_launch_proc` (`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_launch_procs.py:81-89`), which only diverts to `_submit_remote_fork` when `display_name.startswith("Fork on ")`. But every caller passes a prefixed name: `_launch_submission.py:331` passes `f"launch {ctx.display_name}"`, `_launch_bulk.py:190` passes `f"launch {plan.display_name}"`, and `_fleet_dispatch_launches.py:89` passes `f"check launch {alias}"`. The intercept never fires.
5. Result: the fork instruction is submitted as a brand-new LOCAL agent on the controller, and `_pending_remote_fork_identity` is never cleared (it can hijack a later unrelated launch whose name happens to match).

The only test (`tests/ace/tui/test_remote_lifecycle_actions.py:153-159`) asserts the prompt bar opens and stops there, so the dead branch is untested.

issue.creation_reason: A remote fork silently runs on the controller instead of the owner, which is the worst failure for a low-resource viewer machine, and no bead tracked it.
